# Quai

> Quai puts a self-hosted media stack (Seerr, Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, Jellyfin, Cleanuparr, Reclaimerr) on the iPhone's Lock Screen. Live Activities follow each movie or episode from the request to "ready to watch", and what plays on Jellyfin. Notifications say when something breaks and when it's fixed. It has two parts: Quai Home, which runs on your server and keeps your keys and data, and Quai Cloud, which sends the pushes through Apple. Use our hosted Quai Cloud (free during the beta) or run your own. Open source (Apache-2.0). The iPhone app is in beta on TestFlight, iPhone only, iOS 26 or later.

- Website: https://quai.stream
- iPhone app (TestFlight public beta): https://testflight.apple.com/join/RpYX68mQ
- Source code: https://github.com/mathieuletyrant/quai-app
- Support: https://quai.stream/support, support@quai.stream
- Community and help (Discord): https://discord.gg/ytrjjGXTKZ
- Privacy policy: https://quai.stream/privacy
- Bugs and ideas: https://github.com/mathieuletyrant/quai-app/issues

## What Quai does

- **Download Live Activity**: from the moment a title is added, on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island: searching, downloading (percent, speed, time left, from qBittorrent), importing, ready to watch. A season pack keeps its name while its episodes import one by one. When Radarr or Sonarr can't import a download on its own, the activity turns grey and says so until it's imported. "Ready to watch" comes once Jellyfin has the title, matched by any id both know (TMDB, TVDB or IMDb; Jellyfin has no TVDB id without its plugin), whatever Jellyfin names it.
- **Request Live Activity**: a Seerr request waiting for approval, with Approve and Decline buttons on the Lock Screen.
- **Playback Live Activity**: what plays on Jellyfin, time left, Play/Pause from the Lock Screen.
- **Today Live Activity**: today's episodes and movies with their air time, ticked off as they arrive.
- **Alerts**: one notification when a problem starts and one when it's over: a service that stops answering, the media disk running low, a health problem Radarr, Sonarr or Prowlarr report, a deletion Reclaimerr plans.
- **Gone**: one notification once something Upcoming showed as going has happened: a title Reclaimerr deleted (or moved), a stuck download Cleanuparr removed, a torrent its download cleaner took out of qBittorrent after seeding, with the space that came back when it surely did. Off until turned on, per kind, in the app's Settings → Notifications; only what happened within the hour is notified, the rest goes to the Journal. A title let go in Quai is still notified once gone.
- **The app**: a floating bar over the tabs with what plays and every title on its way (searching, downloading, importing); Home (what to fix, requests waiting, Upcoming, alerts, the latest titles added, how many are wanted, disk space), Upcoming (what the stack will do on its own, by date: the releases Radarr and Sonarr will grab in the next 14 days, the deletions Reclaimerr plans, the downloads Cleanuparr will remove and the finished torrents its download cleaner will take out of qBittorrent, each with the space that really comes back once the last hardlinked copy goes), Library (movies and series with posters, what's missing), To fix (blocked imports, titles with no release, deletions coming, downloads Cleanuparr is about to remove), Search (a movie or a series typed or said out loud, found in Seerr and requested in a tap; a series asks which seasons).
- **Search from the Lock Screen**: a control (Lock Screen, Control Center, Action button) opens the search already listening, and a Lock Screen widget opens it with the keyboard up; Dictation runs on the iPhone when it can: only the text goes to the server.
- **Upcoming's seed cleanups and freed space** need Quai Home 0.28 or later (protocol 9): it reads Cleanuparr's download cleaner rules and whether Radarr and Sonarr import with hardlinks. With an older Quai Home, Upcoming shows the releases, deletions and stuck removals, and says to update it.
- **Request as**: in the app's Settings, each iPhone picks the Seerr user its requests are made for (Seerr's admin by default), so that person's auto-approval and quotas apply. Needs Quai Home 0.27 or later (protocol 8); an older one makes the app say to update it.
- **The web console** (served by Quai Home): set the services, shape each Live Activity as a flow (its steps and what each shows, with a preview and a Test button), set the alerts, pair and remove iPhones, read the Journal of what Quai did.

Live Activities run even with the app closed: they are started and updated by pushes from Quai Cloud.

## How it works

```
 your server                                   anywhere
+-------------------------------+         +-----------------+          +--------+
| Seerr · Radarr · Sonarr       |         |                 |  Apple   |        |
| Prowlarr · qBittorrent        | ------> |   Quai Cloud    | -------> | iPhone |
| Jellyfin · Cleanuparr         | <------ | (stores nothing)| <------- |        |
| Reclaimerr      ^             |         |                 |   app    |        |
|                 |             |         +-----------------+          +--------+
|             Quai Home         |
|      (your keys, your data)   |
+-------------------------------+
```

- **Quai Home** runs next to your services. It holds their addresses and API keys, the paired iPhones, the flows, the alert settings and a 7-day journal, in its `/data` volume. It sets up the Radarr, Sonarr and Seerr webhooks itself, polls only what's needed, and only makes calls on a fixed allowlist. It connects *out* to Quai Cloud over a WebSocket: no port to open for the Cloud.
- **Quai Cloud** runs the flows and sends the pushes to Apple Push Notification service. It stores nothing: no database, nothing on disk. When Quai Home connects, the Cloud loads what it needs from it. It never receives your services' addresses or API keys.
- **The iPhone app** pairs with your Quai Home by scanning a QR code shown in the console. There is no account. The app talks to Quai Cloud, which relays to your Quai Home.

## Choose your setup

| | Hosted Quai Cloud | Fully self-hosted |
|---|---|---|
| You run | Quai Home | Quai Home and Quai Cloud |
| Works with the TestFlight app | Yes, with Live Activities and notifications | Pairing works, but no Live Activities or notifications: see below |
| Apple developer account | Not needed | Needed: your own push key and your own build of the app |
| Away from home | Works out of the box | Needs a public address for your Quai Cloud |
| Cost | Free during the beta | Your server |

Why a self-hosted Cloud needs its own app build: Apple only accepts pushes signed with the push key of the app's own developer account. The hosted Cloud holds Quai's key, so it can push to the TestFlight app. A Cloud of your own must use your key, which only works with the app built and signed under your own Apple developer account.

## Setup 1: Quai Home with the hosted Quai Cloud (recommended)

Requirements: a server that runs Docker (or Umbrel), your media apps on it, an iPhone with iOS 26.

1. Run Quai Home:

   ```yaml
   services:
     quai-home:
       image: ghcr.io/mathieuletyrant/quai-home:latest
       restart: unless-stopped
       ports: ["8788:8788"]
       environment:
         QUAI_CLOUD_URL: wss://cloud.quai.stream/home
         QUAI_HOME_PASSWORD: change-me
         QUAI_INTERNAL_URL: http://<server-address>:8788
       volumes:
         - ./quai-home:/data
   ```

   ```sh
   docker compose up -d
   ```

   - `QUAI_CLOUD_URL` links Quai Home to the hosted Quai Cloud.
   - `QUAI_HOME_PASSWORD` protects the console. Without it, the console stays locked.
   - `QUAI_INTERNAL_URL` is how Radarr, Sonarr and Seerr reach Quai Home, for the webhooks it sets up in them. Use an address they can reach: the server's LAN address, or the container's name if they share a Docker network (`http://quai-home:8788`).

2. Open the console at `http://<server-address>:8788` and sign in with `QUAI_HOME_PASSWORD`.
3. **Settings**: Quai Cloud shows "Connected".
4. **Services**: for each service you use, enter its address as Quai Home reaches it and its API key. Each key is checked as you save it, and each service should read "Connected".
5. Install the app from TestFlight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/RpYX68mQ
6. **iPhones → Pair an iPhone** in the console shows a QR code. Scan it with the iPhone's Camera app: it opens Quai and pairs. Allow Live Activities and notifications when asked.
7. **Flows**: check that the Live Activities you want are enabled, and use a flow's **Test** button to send one to your iPhone.

Away from home there is nothing more to do: the app reaches the hosted Quai Cloud at `https://cloud.quai.stream`, which relays to your Quai Home over its link.

To also open the console from outside, put Quai Home's port 8788 behind your own proxy or tunnel and add `QUAI_CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL: https://quai.example.com` to its environment before pairing. The app's "Open the console" then opens the local console at home and this address when out. See "Reaching the console away from home" below.

## Setup 2: Umbrel

1. In umbrelOS, App Store → Community App Stores, add `https://github.com/mathieuletyrant/umbrel-community-app-store`, then install **Quai**.
2. In the app's settings in umbrelOS, set **QUAI_CLOUD_URL** to `wss://cloud.quai.stream/home` for the hosted Quai Cloud. The default, `ws://mathieu-quai_cloud_1:8787/home`, is the Quai Cloud bundled in the app, which needs your own Apple push key and app build (see Setup 3).
3. Open Quai and sign in with the default password umbrelOS shows for the app.
4. **Services**: the Umbrel addresses of Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyfin, Seerr, Prowlarr, Cleanuparr and Reclaimerr are already filled in. Paste each API key. For qBittorrent, use `http://qbittorrent_server_1:8080`, or `http://mathieu-qbittorrent-vpn_gluetun_1:8080` for qBittorrent VPN, with its password.
5. **iPhones → Pair an iPhone**, and scan the QR code.
6. Optional: to open the console from outside, put the app behind your own proxy or tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel with Access, Tailscale…) and set **QUAI_CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL** in the app's settings to that address, then pair again. With the hosted Quai Cloud, the Quai Cloud settings of the app (`QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_URL`, `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_HEADERS`, the Apple key) are not used.

## Setup 3: fully self-hosted (Quai Home and your own Quai Cloud)

For developers with an Apple developer account. You build the iPhone app yourself, with your own bundle id and push key.

1. In your Apple developer account, create a push key (Keys → Apple Push Notifications service) and note its Key ID and your Team ID.
2. Build the app from `apps/ios` in the repository with your own team and bundle id (`pnpm gen:client && cd apps/ios && xcodegen generate`, then open `Quai.xcodeproj`).
3. Run both images:

   ```yaml
   services:
     cloud:
       image: ghcr.io/mathieuletyrant/quai:latest
       restart: unless-stopped
       ports: ["8787:8787"]
       environment:
         QUAI_APNS_KEY_FILE: /keys/AuthKey.p8
         QUAI_APNS_KEY_ID: ABCDE12345
         QUAI_APNS_TEAM_ID: FGHIJ67890
         QUAI_APNS_TOPIC: com.example.quai
       volumes: ["./keys:/keys:ro"]
     home:
       image: ghcr.io/mathieuletyrant/quai-home:latest
       restart: unless-stopped
       ports: ["8788:8788"]
       environment:
         QUAI_CLOUD_URL: ws://cloud:8787/home
         QUAI_CLOUD_APP_URL: http://<server-address>:8787
         QUAI_HOME_PASSWORD: change-me
         QUAI_INTERNAL_URL: http://home:8788
       volumes: ["./data:/data"]
   ```

   `QUAI_CLOUD_APP_URL` is where the iPhone reaches your Quai Cloud at home. It goes into the pairing QR code, because `ws://cloud:8787` only works inside Docker.

4. Follow steps 2 to 7 of Setup 1, with your own build of the app.
5. To use the app away from home, put Quai Cloud behind a reverse proxy and set `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_URL` (and `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_HEADERS` if the proxy requires headers, such as a Cloudflare Access service token). Both go into the pairing QR code. Details: https://github.com/mathieuletyrant/quai-app/blob/main/docs/proxy.md
6. If `/home` can be reached from outside your network, set `QUAI_HOME_ID` to your home's id (the 32 hex characters Quai Home logs as `linked as home …`), so no other Quai Home can use your Cloud and push key.

## Reaching the console away from home

The console is served by Quai Home (port 8788), behind `QUAI_HOME_PASSWORD`. It is not on Quai Cloud, hosted or not. To open it from outside, put Quai Home behind your own reverse proxy or tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel with Access, Tailscale, Pangolin…), and set `QUAI_CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL` on Quai Home to that address. The pairing QR code carries the address the console was opened at and this public one; the app's "Open the console" opens the first that answers, so the local one at home and the public one when out. `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_URL` is unrelated: it is the address of a self-hosted Quai Cloud for the app.

## Configuration reference

### Quai Home

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `QUAI_CLOUD_URL` | The Quai Cloud's WebSocket: `wss://cloud.quai.stream/home` for the hosted one, `ws://cloud:8787/home` for your own. Without it, Quai Home runs alone and its console says what to set. |
| `QUAI_CLOUD_APP_URL` | Where the iPhone reaches Quai Cloud at home, for the pairing QR code, when `QUAI_CLOUD_URL` is an address only Quai Home reaches. Default: `QUAI_CLOUD_URL` in http(s), without `/home`. |
| `QUAI_HOME_PASSWORD` | The console's password. Without it, the console stays locked. |
| `QUAI_CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL` | The console's address from outside, behind your own proxy or tunnel. Added to the pairing QR code for the app's "Open the console". |
| `QUAI_HOME_PORT` | The console, the webhooks and `/health`. Default `8788`. |
| `QUAI_INTERNAL_URL` | How Radarr, Sonarr and Seerr reach Quai Home, for the webhooks it sets up. |
| `QUAI_DATA_DIR` | Where Quai Home keeps its data. `/data` in the image. |
| `QUAI_RADARR_URL`, `QUAI_RADARR_API_KEY` | Radarr (key in Settings → General). |
| `QUAI_SONARR_URL`, `QUAI_SONARR_API_KEY` | Sonarr (key in Settings → General). |
| `QUAI_RADARR_WEB_URL`, `QUAI_RADARR_PUBLIC_URL` | Optional: where the iPhone opens Radarr, at home and from outside ("Open in Radarr"). |
| `QUAI_SONARR_WEB_URL`, `QUAI_SONARR_PUBLIC_URL` | The same for Sonarr. |
| `QUAI_JELLYFIN_URL`, `QUAI_JELLYFIN_API_KEY` | Jellyfin (Dashboard → API Keys). |
| `QUAI_QBITTORRENT_URL`, `QUAI_QBITTORRENT_USERNAME`, `QUAI_QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD` | qBittorrent Web UI. |
| `QUAI_SEERR_URL`, `QUAI_SEERR_API_KEY` | Seerr, Jellyseerr or Overseerr (Settings → General). |
| `QUAI_PROWLARR_URL`, `QUAI_PROWLARR_API_KEY` | Prowlarr (Settings → General), for the alerts. |
| `QUAI_RECLAIMERR_URL`, `QUAI_RECLAIMERR_API_KEY` | Reclaimerr (Settings → Integrations, scopes `candidates:manage` and `system:read`; add `events:read` to be notified of what it deleted). |
| `QUAI_CLEANUPARR_URL`, `QUAI_CLEANUPARR_API_KEY` | Cleanuparr (Settings → Account). |

Every service can be set in the console's **Services** page instead of the environment. A variable set in the environment wins and shows as "Env" there. A service set in neither place is skipped.

### Quai Cloud (self-hosted only)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `QUAI_PORT` | `8787` | The app's API (`/api`) and Quai Home's WebSocket (`/home`). |
| `QUAI_APNS_KEY_FILE` or `QUAI_APNS_KEY` | | Your Apple push key: a path to the `.p8` file, or its text. |
| `QUAI_APNS_KEY_ID`, `QUAI_APNS_TEAM_ID` | | The key's id and your team id. |
| `QUAI_APNS_TOPIC` | `com.mathieuletyrant.quai` | Your app's bundle id. |
| `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_URL` | | The Cloud's address from outside, added to the pairing QR code. |
| `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_HEADERS` | | Headers your reverse proxy requires from the app: `Name: value` pairs separated by `;`. |
| `QUAI_TZ` | `UTC` | Time zone for "today", until an iPhone reports its own. |
| `QUAI_HOME_ID` | | The only Quai Homes served, comma-separated; any other is refused. |
| `QUAI_MAX_HOMES` | | How many Quai Homes may be linked at once. |

### Images

- Quai Home: `ghcr.io/mathieuletyrant/quai-home` (tags `latest`, `X.Y`, `X.Y.Z`), linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
- Quai Cloud: `ghcr.io/mathieuletyrant/quai` (same tags).
- Update Quai Home and a self-hosted Quai Cloud together: they speak a versioned protocol. The hosted Cloud follows each release.

## Troubleshooting

- **No Live Activity shows up**: check iPhone Settings → Quai → Live Activities, that the flow is enabled in the console under Flows, and that Quai Cloud reads "Connected" in the console. Then use the flow's Test button. With a self-hosted Cloud, check that the Apple push key reads "Ready" in Settings.
- **The app doesn't connect away from home**: with the hosted Cloud, check that Quai Home is linked (console → Settings). With your own Cloud, set `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_URL` (and `QUAI_CLOUD_PUBLIC_HEADERS`) and pair the iPhone again.
- **A service isn't connected**: check its address (as Quai Home reaches it, inside Docker) and its API key under Services. A service marked "Env" is set in Quai Home's environment, which wins over the page.
- **Seerr requests arrive late**: if Seerr's webhook already posts somewhere else, Quai leaves it and checks requests regularly instead. The Journal says so.
- **"Quai Home went offline" in the Journal**: Quai Home lost its link to Quai Cloud for more than a minute (shorter drops, which happen a few times a day with the hosted Cloud, are reconnections and aren't logged). Webhooks that arrive meanwhile wait in Quai Home and are sent once it's back. Check that Quai Home is running and reaches the internet.
- **A Live Activity updates slowly**: iOS limits how often Live Activities refresh, more so in Low Power Mode. Quai sends an update at each step and regularly during a download.
- **No alerts**: check iPhone Settings → Notifications → Quai, the mute options in the app's Settings, and the alert's switch in the console under Alerts.
- **No notification when Reclaimerr deletes a title**: turn on "Reclaimerr deleted a title" under Gone in the app's Settings → Notifications, give Reclaimerr's key the `events:read` scope (the console's Services page says when it lacks it), and update Quai Home (it needs protocol 10).
- **"Open the console" is missing in the app, or doesn't work away from home**: set `QUAI_CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL` on Quai Home to the console's address from outside, then pair the iPhone again from the console.
- **Remove Quai**: remove each iPhone under iPhones, then uninstall Quai Home (it removes its webhooks from your services), and delete the app.

Ask on the Discord (https://discord.gg/ytrjjGXTKZ) or write to support@quai.stream. When reporting a bug, include the app's build number (TestFlight), Quai Home's version (bottom of the console), whether the Cloud is hosted or self-hosted, what you did and what you expected, and the Journal lines from around that time.

## Privacy

- Your services' addresses, API keys, library and journal stay in Quai Home, on your server. Quai Home never sends addresses or keys to any Quai Cloud.
- The hosted Quai Cloud receives only the content of each update (a title, an episode, a step, a percentage, the name of a service that is down) and the iPhones' Apple push tokens. It forwards updates to Apple and keeps nothing on disk. Push tokens are held in memory while your Quai Home is connected. It runs on Cloudflare, in the European Union.
- No account, no analytics, no ads, no tracking, no third-party SDK in the app.
- The website, quai.stream, counts its visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, without cookies.
- Full policy: https://quai.stream/privacy

## Limits of the beta

- iPhone only, iOS 26 or later. No iPad, Mac or Android app.
- Playback works with Jellyfin; Plex and Emby are not supported.
- TestFlight builds expire after 90 days; new ones install on their own.
- The hosted Quai Cloud is free during the beta.
